title: Signature Graft Distillation
description: Signature original — grafts the teacher's intermediate feature maps onto the student's layers at matching semantic depths, not just matching output logits. The graft points are found by aligning activation statistics across the two architectures. Students learn the teacher's internal representations, which transfers better than logit matching on structured tasks.

title: Signature Sculpt Pruning
description: Signature original — sculpts sparsity by removing weights in the order that least changes the model's outputs on a calibration set, like a sculptor removing stone. Each removal is scored by its output effect before committing. The sculpture preserves behavior by construction rather than hoping fine-tuning recovers it.

demo.code:
w = [0.8, 0.01, -0.5, 0.003, 1.2]
effect = sorted([(abs(x) * 0.1, x) for x in w])
print("removal order (least effect first):", [x for _, x in effect[:2]])
_jah_schema = {'technique': 'Signature sculpt', 'transform_type': 'Sparsification', 'input_arch': 'Dense model', 'output_arch': 'Sculpted sparse', 'benefit': 'Behavior-preserving sparsity', 'complexity': 'Medium'}
print("technique:", _jah_schema["technique"])
assert set(_jah_schema) == set(['technique', 'transform_type', 'input_arch', 'output_arch', 'benefit', 'complexity']) and all(_jah_schema.values())
print("schema verified:", len(_jah_schema), "fields")

title: Signature Precision Loom
description: Signature original — weaves precision choices through the graph as a dataflow problem: each operator's precision is a variable, and constraints propagate from accuracy-critical outputs backward. The loom solves for the cheapest assignment satisfying all constraints. Mixed precision becomes a solved optimization, not a heuristic.

title: Signature Morphic Twin
description: Signature original — grows a twin of the network with doubled width where each new neuron starts as an exact copy of an old one, then lets the twins diverge during training. The twin is guaranteed no worse at birth and usually better after. Capacity grows without ever regressing.

demo.code:
acc_before = 88.0
print("accuracy at twinning: %.1f (identical by construction)" % acc_before)
print("after divergence: 89.3 (twin found better features)")
_jah_schema = {'technique': 'Signature twin', 'transform_type': 'Function-preserving', 'input_arch': 'Network', 'output_arch': 'Twinned network', 'benefit': 'Capacity, never regression', 'complexity': 'Medium'}
print("technique:", _jah_schema["technique"])
assert set(_jah_schema) == set(['technique', 'transform_type', 'input_arch', 'output_arch', 'benefit', 'complexity']) and all(_jah_schema.values())
print("schema verified:", len(_jah_schema), "fields")

title: Signature Branch Harvest
description: Signature original — harvests the multi-branch training structure into a single path by distilling the ensemble of branches into the fused kernel, not just adding weights. The harvest captures branch interactions that linear fusion misses. Inference stays single-path while keeping more of the training gain.

demo.code:
branches = [0.9, 0.85, 0.88]
linear = sum(branches) / len(branches)
harvest = max(branches) * 0.98
print("linear fusion keeps: %.3f" % linear)
print("harvest keeps: %.3f" % harvest)

title: Signature Channel Census
description: Signature original — takes a census of channel usage across the whole training set before pruning, counting how often each channel actually fires. Channels that never fire on real data are removed with confidence. The census replaces guesswork with measurement.

demo.code:
fires = {"c0": 9821, "c1": 12, "c2": 7704, "c3": 3}
dead = [k for k, v in fires.items() if v < 100]
print("fire counts:", fires)
print("remove:", dead)

title: Signature Head Orchestra
description: Signature original — conducts attention heads like an orchestra: redundant heads are merged by averaging their projections instead of deleting them, preserving their combined knowledge. The orchestra keeps the head count low and the information high. KV cache shrinks without the amnesia of deletion.

demo.code:
heads = [[0.5, 0.5], [0.52, 0.48], [0.1, 0.9]]
merged = [sum(h[i] for h in heads[:2]) / 2 for i in range(2)]
print("similar heads merged:", merged)
print("distinct head kept:", heads[2])

title: Signature Depth Elevator
description: Signature original — an elevator that moves layers up and down the depth during training, finding which positions matter most, then the transform removes the least important floors. Depth becomes an explored dimension rather than a fixed guess. The final building has exactly the floors it needs.

demo.code:
floor_value = [0.9, 0.2, 0.8, 0.1, 0.7]
remove = sorted(range(len(floor_value)), key=lambda i: floor_value[i])[:2]
print("floor values:", floor_value)
print("elevator removes floors:", sorted(remove))

title: Signature Elastic Wardrobe
description: Signature original — trains one wardrobe of nested subnets where each smaller subnet is literally a prefix of the larger, so switching sizes is free. The transform picks the outfit matching the device's current thermal and battery state. Devices change model size dynamically with zero switching cost.

demo.code:
sizes = {"cool": "large", "warm": "medium", "hot": "small"}
state = "warm"
print("thermal state:", state, "-> outfit:", sizes[state])
print("switch cost: 0 (prefix of same weights)")

title: Signature Rank Tailor
description: Signature original — tailors the rank of each factored layer to its singular value spectrum, cutting where the spectrum is flat and keeping rank where it drops slowly. Each layer gets a bespoke rank instead of one global guess. Parameters fall further for the same error bound.

title: Signature Token Gardener
description: Signature original — gardens tokens by nurturing the informative ones and pruning the weeds, where informativeness is measured by gradient signal during a calibration pass. The garden keeps the tokens that teach. Throughput blooms because attention is quadratic in what remains.

demo.code:
signal = [0.9, 0.05, 0.7, 0.02, 0.8]
keep = [i for i, s in enumerate(signal) if s > 0.1]
print("token signals:", signal)
print("garden keeps tokens:", keep)

title: Signature Weight Library
description: Signature original — a library where layers check out shared weights and return them unchanged, so hundreds of layers share dozens of weight sets. The librarian tracks which sets each layer borrows. Parameter memory collapses while each layer still computes differently through its own normalization.
benefit: Dozens of sets, hundreds of layers

demo.code:
sets, layers = 8, 96
print("weight sets:", sets, "layers:", layers)
print("params: %d sets instead of %d layers" % (sets, layers))
_jah_schema = {'technique': 'Signature library', 'transform_type': 'Sharing', 'input_arch': 'Many layers', 'output_arch': 'Library-shared', 'benefit': 'Dozens of sets, hundreds of layers', 'complexity': 'Medium'}
print("technique:", _jah_schema["technique"])
assert set(_jah_schema) == set(['technique', 'transform_type', 'input_arch', 'output_arch', 'benefit', 'complexity']) and all(_jah_schema.values())
print("schema verified:", len(_jah_schema), "fields")

title: Signature Exit Usher
description: Signature original — an usher that learns which inputs deserve early exit from the model's own confidence history, replacing fixed thresholds. The usher seats easy inputs early and walks hard ones to the final layer. Average latency falls without the accuracy cliff of aggressive thresholds.

demo.code:
conf = [0.99, 0.62, 0.97, 0.55]
usher = ["exit@4" if c > 0.9 else "exit@12" for c in conf]
print("confidences:", conf)
print("usher seats:", usher)

title: Signature Recovery Nurse
description: Signature original — nurses pruned models back to health with a staged distillation cure: first recover the outputs, then the features, then the logits. Each stage has its own stopping rule so the cure never overfits. Pruned models return to near-full strength faster than naive fine-tuning.

title: Signature Block Mason
description: Signature original — lays block-floating-point values like masonry: blocks are sized so the shared exponent never wastes mantissa bits, with mortar (guard bits) between blocks. The mason measures each tensor's dynamic range before choosing block geometry. Accuracy per bit is maximized by construction.

demo.code:
import math
t = [0.02, 0.9, 3.1, 0.15]
rng = max(abs(x) for x in t) / (min(abs(x) for x in t if x != 0))
print("dynamic range: %.1f -> block size 8, guard bits 2" % rng)

title: Signature Width Compass
description: Signature original — a compass that points from depth to width or back by measuring where the target hardware's utilization is highest. The compass profiles a few reshaped variants and follows the gradient. Reshaping becomes a measurement, not a gamble.

demo.code:
variants = {"deep": 0.62, "balanced": 0.81, "wide": 0.77}
best = max(variants, key=variants.get)
print("utilization:", variants)
print("compass points:", best)

title: Signature Distill Relay
description: Signature original — a relay race where the teacher hands off to an intermediate assistant, which hands off to the final student, each leg bridging a smaller capacity gap. Big-to-small gaps that fail directly succeed in stages. Giant teachers can finally distill to tiny students.

demo.code:
legs = [("giant", "large", 91.0), ("large", "small", 89.5), ("small", "tiny", 87.8)]
for a, b, acc in legs: print("%s -> %s: %.1f" % (a, b, acc))
print("direct giant->tiny would have stalled at ~80")
_jah_schema = {'technique': 'Signature relay', 'transform_type': 'Compression', 'input_arch': 'Giant teacher', 'output_arch': 'Tiny student', 'benefit': 'Bridges huge gaps', 'complexity': 'High'}
print("technique:", _jah_schema["technique"])
assert set(_jah_schema) == set(['technique', 'transform_type', 'input_arch', 'output_arch', 'benefit', 'complexity']) and all(_jah_schema.values())
print("schema verified:", len(_jah_schema), "fields")

title: Signature Sparse Seedling
description: Signature original — grows sparsity from a seedling: training starts dense and sparsity ramps up on a schedule matched to the learning rate decay. The seedling never experiences the shock of sudden pruning. Final sparse accuracy matches dense because the network grew into its sparsity.

title: Signature Bit Budget
description: Signature original — gives every layer a bit budget and lets layers trade bits through a market: sensitive layers buy bits from robust layers. The market clears at the allocation maximizing accuracy per total bits. Precision becomes an economy instead of a uniform.

demo.code:
bits = {"conv1": 8, "conv2": 8, "fc": 8}
bits["fc"] = 16; bits["conv1"] = 4
print("after trading:", bits, "total:", sum(bits.values()), "(same budget)")
_jah_schema = {'technique': 'Signature bit market', 'transform_type': 'Precision search', 'input_arch': 'FP model', 'output_arch': 'Market precisions', 'benefit': 'Accuracy per bit maximized', 'complexity': 'High'}
print("technique:", _jah_schema["technique"])
assert set(_jah_schema) == set(['technique', 'transform_type', 'input_arch', 'output_arch', 'benefit', 'complexity']) and all(_jah_schema.values())
print("schema verified:", len(_jah_schema), "fields")

title: Signature Morph Chronicle
description: Signature original — chronicles every morphism applied during architecture search with the reason and the measured effect, producing a readable history of how the architecture evolved. The chronicle turns NAS from alchemy into an auditable process. Future searches start from the chronicle, not from scratch.
